title: Beyond the Milkman: AI’s New Playbook for Medtech Commercial Excellence
gist: BCG benchmarking argues medtech firms that modernized commercial models earned 8 points higher annual TSR than the MSCI health care equipment index, and that AI is the next stage, via five moves (targeting, personalization, augmented/autonomous sales, pricing, 24/7 service) on one data and intelligence platform. A diagnostics case projects +2 points EBITDA; most value (70%) is claimed to come from process and behavior change.

insights.claim: Medtech companies that built next-generation commercial models delivered annual TSR eight percentage points above the MSCI Health Care Equipment and Supplies Index, even as sector returns came under pressure.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/goetz-gerecke
entities: MSCI Health Care Equipment and Supplies Index
insights.so_what: Commercial capability is a measurable alpha factor within medtech.

insights.claim: Earlier BCG studies (2017 and 2021) found adopters of recommended commercial moves earned about ten percentage points higher shareholder returns than peers, a pattern held over 15 years and four benchmarking studies.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/goetz-gerecke
insights.so_what: Consistent but self-reported consultancy data; treat as directional.

insights.claim: Most medtech executives still rate their next-generation commercial capabilities as only basic to intermediate, so slow adoption leaves a gap that early movers exploit.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/goetz-gerecke
insights.so_what: Most of the sector lags, so laggards face rerating risk and leaders keep an edge.

insights.claim: The legacy 'milkman' model of frequent in-person rep visits was masked by high gross margins that hid unsustainable commercial costs and underdeveloped skills.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/goetz-gerecke
insights.so_what: Gross margin pressure exposes inefficient sales models.

insights.claim: AI lets medtech make commercial operations leaner and more productive at once, lifting margins while raising revenue, whereas traditional levers either cut cost or accelerated growth.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/goetz-gerecke
insights.so_what: Supports margin expansion plus growth rather than cost-cutting stories.

insights.claim: Cost reduction alone is insufficient for long-term shareholder returns in medtech; accelerating profitable growth is the bigger priority.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/goetz-gerecke
insights.so_what: Favor growth-investing medtech over pure cost-out stories.

insights.claim: Medtech faces stricter regulation, public cost pressure, payer and provider consolidation, tariff uncertainty, and low-cost entrants taking share from incumbents.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/goetz-gerecke
insights.so_what: Defines the headwinds that make commercial efficiency matter.

insights.claim: The sector is supported by aging demographics, improved access, and consumerization of health care.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/goetz-gerecke
insights.so_what: Structural demand backdrop remains resilient.

themes.theme: Five AI commercial moves and quantified impact

insights.claim: Real-time 360-degree buyer views with dynamic targeting can often double relevant leads for sales teams and raise conversion rates by 30% to 50% on average.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/goetz-gerecke
insights.so_what: Lead and conversion lift is the headline top-line case.

insights.claim: AI shifts customer tracking from account level to individual buyer level, streaming in data from reps, service, web activity, and email responses.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/goetz-gerecke
insights.so_what: Individual-level data is the new asset.

insights.claim: AI marketing enables segmentation to collapse to a segment of one, with modular content assembled per buyer, e.g. a surgeon versus a procurement-minded hospital administrator, under governance on clinical and regulatory claims.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/goetz-gerecke
insights.so_what: Compliance-bound personalization is a gating feature.

insights.claim: Augmented and autonomous selling can reduce turnover of critical sales talent and increase conversion rates by 30% to 50% using the existing commercial organization.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/goetz-gerecke
insights.so_what: Growth without headcount adds operating leverage.

insights.claim: Autonomous selling could involve a GenAI system executing commercial interactions itself, potentially working directly with a customer's procurement agent.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/goetz-gerecke
insights.so_what: Agent-to-agent B2B negotiation is a potential future channel.

insights.claim: Data-driven pricing transformations have delivered 7% to 12% gross margin improvements within the first year.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/goetz-gerecke
insights.so_what: Pricing is the highest-leverage margin lever.

insights.claim: Medtech pricing is underdeveloped: list prices are negotiated down by discretionary discounting, reps move in coarse five-point increments, and managers are often incentivized on top-line only, so volume is prioritized over value.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/goetz-gerecke
insights.so_what: Incentive design explains persistent margin leakage.

insights.claim: BCG found B2B pricing teams across industries typically spend three out of five days on pricing admin and management.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/goetz-gerecke
insights.so_what: Automation headroom in pricing back-office is large.

insights.claim: A pricing and margin engine reveals true account profitability, which should set how much commercial effort and cost to spend serving each account.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/goetz-gerecke
insights.so_what: Links price realization to resource allocation.

insights.claim: 24/7 agentic service cuts turnaround times 20% to 50%, queue times 30% to 50%, and delivers double-digit reductions in cost-to-serve; after-hours service interactions can also surface buying signals as leads.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/goetz-gerecke
insights.so_what: Service AI both cuts cost and feeds sales pipeline.

themes.theme: The platform backbone and compounding data advantage

insights.claim: Leading firms build all AI commercial moves on one three-layer backbone (data layer, intelligence layer, AI-orchestrated channels) rather than dozens of disconnected apps.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/goetz-gerecke
insights.so_what: Platform integration, not point solutions, drives value.

insights.claim: As AI-enabled software development gets easier, differentiation will come from proprietary commercial data, domain-specific business logic, and deep process embedding rather than the algorithms themselves.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/goetz-gerecke
insights.so_what: Moats lie in data and workflow, not models.

insights.claim: The system is self-reinforcing: each new application raises the value of existing ones, and better data, intelligence, and interactions create a feedback loop described as one of the strongest competitive advantages.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/goetz-gerecke
insights.so_what: Compounding learning favors early movers.

insights.claim: Leaders do not wait for perfect data integration or replace existing systems; they consolidate sources into a common commercial view pragmatically.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/goetz-gerecke
insights.so_what: Lower IT replacement spend than feared.

insights.claim: A global diagnostics company with about 300 sales reps and tens of thousands of customers consolidated CRM, purchasing, installed-base, and service data into one platform with next-best-action recommendations, doubling the likelihood customers act on recommendations.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/goetz-gerecke
insights.so_what: Concrete operating example of the platform model.

insights.claim: Its AI portal cut customer request response times from up to six days to minutes.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/goetz-gerecke
insights.so_what: Large service speed gain.

insights.claim: AI pricing recommendations and negotiation simulators raised price adoption by 1.5 percentage points in the annual adjustment.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/goetz-gerecke
insights.so_what: Price realization uplift is quantifiable.

insights.claim: The company expects AI to raise EBITDA by two percentage points, about three times the total capex required, with minimal incremental operating costs.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/goetz-gerecke
insights.so_what: Implies attractive ROI on commercial AI, though it is a projection.

insights.claim: Only about 10% of AI value comes from algorithms, 20% from data and technology, and 70% from reshaping processes, ways of working, and governance.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/goetz-gerecke
insights.so_what: Execution and change management determine returns, not model choice.

insights.claim: Pilots and incremental use cases almost never create material impact; value requires a few bold bets that reshape workflows, management layers, and incentives.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/goetz-gerecke
insights.so_what: Be skeptical of firms touting many pilots.
insights.locator: Be bold and start with value

insights.claim: AI should be a CEO-led business transformation rather than a technology initiative.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/goetz-gerecke
insights.so_what: Leadership ownership is a screen for credible AI adopters.

insights.claim: Agent autonomy is a design choice on a spectrum from agent-assisted to human-in-the-loop, human-on-the-loop, and fully human-out-of-the-loop; medtech will likely keep most agents at the supervised end due to clinical and regulatory exposure.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/goetz-gerecke
insights.so_what: Regulation slows full autonomy, limiting near-term labor substitution.
insights.locator: Three Critical Factors for Agentic Marketing, Sales, and Customer Service

insights.claim: Accountability for AI agent performance should sit with a named person in commercial excellence or operations, and agents need guardrails, escalation paths when confidence is low, and monitoring for drift, error, and hallucination.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/goetz-gerecke
insights.so_what: Governance cost and structure are prerequisites.

insights.claim: AI is expected to augment rather than replace sales reps, and BCG says it makes them happier and more engaged.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/goetz-gerecke
insights.so_what: Positions AI as productivity, not headcount cuts; the claim is author experience.

insights.claim: AI-leading commercial transformers remain a small share of the industry, since applied AI is hard to get right, implying a substantial first-mover advantage.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/goetz-gerecke
insights.so_what: Dispersion between leaders and laggards should widen.

top_entities: MSCI Health Care Equipment and Supplies Index
